_howTo: Radio talks with Walla Walla. Each lesson has two: "start" is typed out on the slip as the lesson opens, and "check" frames the lesson's check: its first line is typed above the check's questions and its last line under the score. In the start talk, each turn has Walla Walla saying "them" and the player picking one of up to three "replies" (none means a plain "Roger. Over."); a reply can have a "back" line, and every reply leads on to the next turn.

turns.them: Harrow, Walla Walla, right on the sked. First lesson tonight, and it starts with the two questions every June brings: will the morning grey burn off, and do the white puffs that come up by mid-morning mean rain?

replies.back: Work through the lesson and tell me. Once you know what a cloud is made of, both questions answer themselves.

turns.them: It goes in order: what a cloud is, how a still night makes fog, and how rising air builds a heap. I’ll come back on at the end with a few questions.
Harrow, Walla Walla again. A few questions over the air, like a Bureau examination, only friendlier. Some photographs first, then some skies.
Fog and heaps, blankets and bubbles: the two textures of the whole sky. Next lesson, grey skies.
